levels_tested: lean 70 to 90%, lard 10 to 30%, starch 0 to 10%
result: Best liked 70% meat, 25% lard, 5% starch; 90% lean least liked; grainy and heterogeneous texture and air holes cut liking; chewy, firm, elastic raise it. 68 consumers aged 18 to 26.
notes: Implication (our inference): textured granules that make a paste grainy are a poor fit for gio and cha; a fine isolate, concentrate or paste is needed.

extender: soy protein concentrate against peanut protein concentrate; 7 commercial sausages containing soy protein
result: Commercial Vietnamese emulsion sausages tested all contained soy protein (7 samples); the same share of consumers were satisfied with the soy control, the peanut versions and two commercial soy sausages.
notes: Abstract only. Confirms soy protein is normal in Vietnamese sausages; says nothing about replacement levels.

extender: modified starch, chitofood, soy germ powder as borax replacers
result: Finished gio lua had 19.1 to 19.4 g protein per 100 g; the paper states that more than 90% of market pork gio lua contained borax or chemical additives (cited claim).
notes: The borax claim is a secondary citation we did not verify; it signals a trust problem around what goes into gio.

extender: soy protein, caseinate, whey, egg albumen, skim milk as binders
result: Soy protein lowered sensory acceptance; whey scored highest; egg albumen, caseinate and whey raised chewiness.
notes: Abstract only. Closest published format to gio lua. Fits Vissan pairing soy with milk protein in gio lua.

product: frankfurter, smoked sausage, fresh pork sausage, ground beef
extender: non-solvent extracted textured soy replacing lean
level_with_no_loss: 15% (smoked sausage); up to 30% for texture and off-flavour in frankfurters
result: 45% gave mushy texture and off-flavour; soy raised off-flavour in all but frankfurters; frankfurter juiciness fell at any level; authors: practical lean replacement below 30%.
25% improved juiciness, tenderness and cooking yield (83.07%); lower redness.

extender: Fusarium venenatum mycoprotein replacing lean pork
result: 25% mycoprotein preferred to the traditional sausage in a ranking test; higher levels lowered preference.
notes: The only fungal biomass in a pork sausage we found.

extender: whole Agaricus bisporus mushroom replacing chicken breast
result: Protein fell from 16.2 to 13.0 g per 100 g, cooking loss rose from 21.4 to 36.1%, texture and sensory scores fell with level; only 10% kept quality.
notes: Whole mushroom (low protein, high water) is not fungal biomass; shows why a mushroom label cannot rest on whole mushrooms at high levels.

product: meatballs and other hybrids at 70% meat, 30% plant
extender: soy, pumpkin, pea as textured protein or high-moisture extrudate
level_with_no_loss: 30% pea textured protein "can still attract consumers"
result: About 50% of consumers would still rather not buy the tasted hybrid; cites UK hybrids above 30% substitution often failing in market.
notes: Market-failure claim is a citation of Grasso and Jaworska 2020 (HXE-12).

result: Blend preferred to plant burgers blind; demand fell when consumers were told the ingredients.
Chicken mince with 30 to 50% plant protein beat 100% chicken; most tasters preferred about 75% animal.
notes: Already in the package; press release level.

study: Search for Vietnamese detection or complaint evidence
result: We found no Vietnamese study measuring whether consumers detect or object to soy or plant protein in gio, cha or sausages (OpenAlex and Scite, 25 Sep 2026). We could not search the press.
notes: Clean negative for the academic record only.
